Area.evidence_source: [page/3/Text/6] Throughout the stories, vulnerability, as well as the courage and strength to carry different loads over time, becomes visible. Eight of the 10 interview subjects tell of events and conditions in early stages of their life, which have contributed to forming their attitudes to themselves and to life in general. 'That was presumably in the beginning, the problems started; it is something about my self-esteem. I have still some of these thoughts, that it is my fault', as one of the interviewees said. Several talked about how incidents and feelings have been 'not-themes' in their life, as loss and grief, like this guy: [page/3/Text/8] Interview subjects reflect on how their inter-relational problems and breaks with important people in their lives, substance abuse, physical injuries and psychological problems, excessive workload, and loss of meaningful tasks in everyday life are affecting their mental health and spirit. One interviewee tells about rape and another about prostitution and how this has affected their self-image. Several said that the idea of suicide came as early as in childhood or in their teen years and was triggered by bullying, identity problems and losses through their parents' divorce, or death of a mother, as in this case: 'I can remember the anxiety, and then the blues started at 9–10 years of age and, as a consequence, I suppose, these thoughts about suicide came creeping in over the teens'.
